title: Lockstep versioning UX hypotheses and copy draft
content:
Context:
This doc collects quick UX hypotheses and wirecopy drafts for a versioning-first flow we're calling "lockstep". Purpose is to give product + eng a single place for lightweight sketches to inform a small prototype (console + API flag) for staged model version adoption and safe rollback during endpoint creation. Not a final spec — just backlog-facing artifacts and copy ideas for user testing.

Goals / success signals:
- Reduce accidental endpoint drift: user should be explicit about which model bundle (model + tokenizer + runtime profile) an endpoint uses.
- Make staged adoption easy: allow a user to create an endpoint that uses a primary model but keeps a warm fallback variant and a rollback policy.
- Surface cost/latency tradeoffs at creation time so teams pick a sensible default.
- Provide a clear undo path (rollback button + audit) with minimal cognitive load.

High-level flow (sketch):
1) Catalog browse -> choose model family -> choose candidate version set (stable / beta / archived)
   - Inline filter chips: "compatible with endpoint config", "low-latency profile available", "quantized"
2) Choose versioning strategy (radio):
   - Staged (default): primary version + canary (0-10% traffic) + fallback
   - Fixed: always use exact version (no automatic swap)
   - Floating: always use latest compatible minor (useful for non-prod)
3) Deployment profile: quick estimate preview shows latency / cost / recommended batch settings
4) Rollout controls: traffic slider (for staged), canary duration, automated regression checks (toggle)
5) Review screen with microcopy, then create endpoint

Wireframe notes (desktop):
- Top bar: left: model breadcrumb (Catalog > llama-3 > v1.2.0), center: quick stats (latency median, tokens/s, cost/1k tokens), right: help icon linking to rollout best practices.
- Middle: large panel split: left (version selector + variants table), right (deployment preview + cost calculator).
- Version selector: vertical list with chips for status (stable/beta/archived), each line has small radio for primary/secondary and an overflow menu for "promote" / "archive notes" / "audit log".
- Variants table header columns: Version | Profile | Avg Latency | Est cost / 1k | Notes | Actions
- Actions: "Set as primary" (radio), "Stage as canary" (chip), "Add fallback" (link)

Copy drafts (high-signal examples):
- Creation header: "Create endpoint: pick a versioning strategy that matches your risk profile"
- Strategy descriptions:
  - Staged (recommended): "Roll out a primary version gradually with a small canary and a warm fallback. Automatic rollback is optional. Good for production with regression checks."
  - Fixed: "Pin this endpoint to an exact model version. No automatic upgrades. Good for reproducibility and audits."
  - Floating: "Keep this endpoint on the latest compatible minor version. Saves ops overhead but may change outputs over time. Use for dev/test."
- Canary tooltip microcopy: "Route a small percentage of traffic to this version to validate quality. We'll show diffs and can auto-rollback on regressions."
- Fallback microcopy: "A warm fallback is kept ready to receive traffic instantly if the primary fails or regresses. Falls back when a policy triggers."
- Review CTA: "Create endpoint and start staged rollout" (primary) and "Create endpoint (pin to version)" (secondary)

Edge cases and error states:
- Catalog shows version but no compatible runtime profile: show inline warning: "No verified runtime for this version in selected region. You can still proceed, but performance may vary."
- Attempting staged rollout with no fallback: block with inline toast: "Staged rollouts require a fallback or an automated circuit breaker. Add a fallback or switch to Fixed."
- Canary failure: show prominent banner in endpoint details with 3 actions: "Rollback now" (immediate), "Pause canary" (stop sending new canary traffic), "View diff" (opens eval-ui)

Observability hooks (console):
- Link to quick diffs: side-by-side sample outputs from primary vs canary for a canonical prompt set (user-supplied or stored eval set).
- Live traffic breakdown: stacked timeline of traffic % per version + 95th latency band per variant.
- Cost preview: estimated monthly cost delta if canary moves to primary (based on token distribution sample).

Backlog items / groom notes (tentative priorities):
- [P0] Small prototype: version selector + staged/fixed/floating radios + review screen (2-wk sprint)
- [P0] API toggle: "versioning_strategy=staged" + rollout config in endpoint Create API (engineer pairing)
- [P1] Canary diff UI: lightweight side-by-side text diffs + token-level delta (3 sprints)
- [P1] Auto-rollback infra hooks (signal definitions: latency, logic_error_rate, hallucination-score from evals)
- [P2] Cost sensitivity slider: "prefer lower cost" vs "prefer lower latency" with suggested profile adjustments

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should staged be default for all orgs or only for orgs with > X tokens/month? (ops risk vs onboarding friction)
- What exact signals will trigger auto-rollback? who owns threshold tuning? (SRE + Applied ML)
- How to represent archived versions in the selector? collapsed by default or shown with a "show archived" toggle?
- Permissions model: who can change primary vs who can only propose (review-only flow)? integrate with existing RBAC.

Suggested user-test script (5–8 users):
- Task 1: Create an endpoint for "llama-3" that will be used in production and should be rolled out gradually. Observe where they look for cost info.
- Task 2: Simulate a failing canary; ask where they expect to see rollback and how they react to the banner.
- Metrics to capture: time-to-create, placement of attention (which panel), error-rate for choosing no fallback, mis-clicks for pin vs floating.

Copy variations to A/B in prototype (short):
- CTA primary: 
  - A: "Create endpoint and start staged rollout"
  - B: "Create endpoint (recommended: staged rollout)"
- Canary label: 
  - A: "Canary (0-10% traffic)"
  - B: "Trial version (small traffic)"

Implementation notes for eng:
- Backend: reuse current endpoint model but add fields: versioning_strategy (enum), canary_config {pct, duration}, fallback_version_id, regression_checks (list of signals).
- DB: small migration to store strategy per endpoint and per-route variant metadata.
- UI: early prototype can store only one fallback + one canary; later expand to weighted multi-variants.
- Telemetry: emit rollout events (start, canary_update, canary_end, rollback, promote) with reasons and deltas.

Next steps (this week):
- Convert this doc to 3 quick Figma frames: catalog-selection, rollout-config, review/create. (Tom)
- Backend sketch of API additions and migration draft. (Jinwoo)
- Schedule brief user interview sessions with 6 internal power users (Marina)

Notes to self / raw brainstorm fragments (keep):
- wonder if "fallback" is anxiety-inducing; maybe use "resilience target" label? try both in test
- allow org policy to default strategy per environment (dev->floating, staging->staged, prod->fixed)
- consider a CLI-first flow where versioning_strategy can be provided at create-time and console just visualizes

Audit trail copy idea (light):
- Banner in endpoint details: "Versioning history: primary set to v1.2.0 by a.patel on 2025-01-24 (staged rollouts: canary 5% until 2025-01-30)"

End of draft.

(If this looks reasonable I'll convert to figma frames and post a short walkthrough in #product-console.)
